properties.chose:
Anthony, 2026-10-14: "let's keep (d) and (e)".
- (d) VALUE AXIOMS MADE EXPLICIT became req:a-conclusion-shows-the-axioms-it-rests-on.
- (e) ARROW'S IMPOSSIBILITY THEOREM AS A TRIAL RUNG joined the ladder in dec:idea-navier-stokes-as-a-trial-of-designing-a-proof. It is the rung that is both mathematics and the design of a system of government, and it tests whether reflow2 makes an impossibility visible.

NOT CHOSEN, kept as considered:
- (a) reading a requirement as a lemma. That is already requirement D (req:the-vocabulary-is-served-in-a-fields-own-terms), so nothing more is needed.
- (b) the golden thread recast as a proof. It may fall out of C and B, and the trials will show whether it does.
- (c) consistency proofs. The Arrow rung will show whether they are worth building.
properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. @ajs, 2026-10-14, "This is mostly me thinking outloud":
"I'm pretty excited for what this means for "design anything" (reflow2's slogan) that it has a mathematical backbone. What is also interesting is when you get into designing things that may be abstract, how a mathematical backbone can help a designer determine a correct solution (based on the idea that the graph is the mathematical proof). Another way to look at this is seeing how mathematical proofs play out in designing something like a new government system for instance. What was once a "requirement" could be replaced by the word "lemme", for instance, and now you can start looking at things in terms of mathematical principles/proofs."

WHAT IS ALREADY SETTLED, so part of this is a HOW:
- req:design-anything (accepted): the vocabulary stays neutral.
- req:the-vocabulary-is-served-in-a-fields-own-terms (D, accepted 2026-10-14) already lets a requirement be READ as a lemma or theorem by an agent or reader who thinks that way. reflow2's own names do not change. Replacing the word would contradict D; reading it in a field's words is D.
- req:a-design-can-be-a-proof (B) and req:a-design-states-how-premises-support-a-conclusion-and-reflow2-checks-it-follows (C) are the machinery.

THE MAPPING THAT HOLDS UP (a sketch): a requirement is a THEOREM ABOUT THE BUILT THING, "the system, as built, meets R". The design is its proof: capabilities satisfy it, verifications pass, and the rule says how they combine. Its premises are EMPIRICAL (tests, measurements), not axioms. So a design proof is CONDITIONAL: if this evidence reflects reality, R is met.

OPTIONS, none chosen:
(a) READING ONLY: a requirement read as a theorem or lemma through D's per-field terms. No new build beyond D.
(b) THE GOLDEN THREAD AS A PROOF: "R is met" is concluded by an Inference over its satisfying capabilities and their passing verifications. C may already make this expressible. A trial would show it.
(c) CONSISTENCY PROOFS: show that a SET of requirements cannot all hold, and name the smallest set to relax. This is what Arrow's impossibility theorem does for voting: with three or more options, no ranked voting rule meets a short list of fairness conditions together. With person-asserted implications it is small; with formal statements and a checker it is large.
(d) VALUE AXIOMS MADE EXPLICIT: in an abstract design (a government, a policy), the chosen principles are recorded as axioms, premises nobody proves. Every conclusion then shows which values it rests on, and changing a value shows what falls (C's broken and weakened).
(e) A LATER TRIAL RUNG THAT IS BOTH MATHEMATICS AND GOVERNMENT DESIGN: Arrow's theorem, which has short known proofs (as recalled: Geanakoplos, "Three brief proofs of Arrow's impossibility theorem"; unchecked), recorded as a design. It shows whether reflow2 makes an impossibility visible.

PUSHBACK, RECORDED BESIDE IT:
- "SHOULD" IS NOT "IS". A requirement is normative: we make it true by building. A lemma is descriptive: it is shown true from axioms. The bridge is the mapping above. The requirement is the CLAIM about the built thing, not the lemma itself, and calling it a lemma outright hides that it is chosen.
- IN A GOVERNMENT, THE AXIOMS ARE VALUES. A proof shows the design follows FROM the chosen principles. It cannot show the principles are right, and they are contested by design (req:a-design-holds-a-line-of-reasoning, "contested, by design").
- EVIDENCE IS NOT PROOF (fact:the-methods-of-proof-mostly-fit-an-inference-and-three-need-more-2026-10-14). Most premises in a real design are measurements and judgements. "Proven correct" would overclaim. The honest phrase is "follows from these principles, given this evidence".
- A STRUCTURE THAT LOOKS PROVEN can lend false confidence to a social question. That is job 3: checks that don't reason say what they do and do not mean.
- WHAT MATHEMATICS GENUINELY ADDS, though, is real: it can PROVE a set of requirements IMPOSSIBLE (Arrow; also the Gibbard–Satterthwaite theorem on strategic voting, and the mechanism-design field). That is a correct, decisive answer a designer cannot get by argument alone.

SIZE (a finding): (a) is D, no more. (b) is a trial on C and B as built. (d) needs nothing new: axioms are premises. (c) is small if the impossibility is asserted by a person, large if derived by a checker. (e) is about one session, like the fundamental-theorem rung.
properties.name: SETTLED 2026-10-14 — "design anything" gets a mathematical backbone through two of its options: value axioms made explicit (d, now a requirement) and Arrow's impossibility theorem as a trial rung (e); the others stay considered
